issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant duplicated across three modules — single source of truth violated
issues.detail: The string 'python:3.12' is now defined in backend/kale/pipeline.py (DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE), hardcoded as a fallback in labextension/src/lib/Commands.ts (return 'python:3.12'), and re-declared in labextension/src/widgets/cell-metadata/CellMetadataEditor.tsx (export const DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE). The whole point of introducing the constant is to have one authoritative definition; instead the abstraction leaks the literal into three places that will silently drift. The ADT here is 'the system's default base image' — its contract must be: exactly one declaration, all callers consult it. Either the backend RPC is the source of truth (and the frontend must not embed a literal), or there is a build-time constant exchange — pick one and enforce it.

issues.description: Semantic contract change in Pipeline._set_base_image silently strengthens postcondition
issues.detail: Previously, when pod introspection failed, self.base_image was set to '' which the downstream template treated as 'fall back to kfp default image'. Now it is set to DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE ('python:3.12'), which is a different postcondition: callers downstream of Pipeline can no longer distinguish 'no image was determined' from 'an explicit image was chosen'. Any subtype, serialization, or consumer that previously branched on empty-string semantics now sees a non-empty string with concrete meaning. This is an LSP-adjacent issue: the Pipeline type's postcondition for base_image has been weakened in observability (cannot tell unset from default) without being declared. State the contract: is base_image now 'always non-empty after _set_base_image()'? If yes, document and enforce that invariant; if no, preserve the empty-string sentinel and resolve the default at render time only.

issues.description: Template fallback chain has redundant rungs after the change — contract is now ambiguous
issues.detail: nb_function_template.jinja2 still evaluates `step.config.base_image or base_image or default_base_image`. But after the pipeline.py change, `base_image` will already be DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE whenever no image was determined, so the third rung is unreachable in practice. Either (a) remove the third rung because `base_image` is now invariantly non-empty, or (b) revert the pipeline.py change and let the template be the single resolution point. The current code has two layers of defaulting with overlapping responsibility — a classic 'where does the contract live' problem.

issues.description: InlineMetadata.createBaseImageText return type changed from string|JSX to always-JSX — interface widened silently
issues.detail:
Previously the method returned either a

element or an empty string ('') when no baseImage was set. Now it unconditionally returns the

element with '(default)' suffix. This is a behavioral change in the rendered DOM for every cell that previously had no base image — those cells now show a 'Base Image: python:3.12 (default)' line they never had before. The component's visual contract has changed for every existing notebook. If that is intentional, fine — but the PR description only promises 'Display default base image in cell metadata UI', not 'add a line to every step cell that previously had none'. Verify this is the intended visual contract.

issues.description: Base Image edit button disabled when stepName is empty — precondition strengthened versus old Input control
issues.detail: The previous Input field for Base Image had no precondition on stepName; users could set the base image regardless. The new IMAGE button has `disabled={!(this.props.stepName && this.props.stepName.length > 0)}`. This strengthens the precondition for editing base_image (now requires a step name) — an LSP-style regression for any workflow where users set image-then-name. Either the precondition was wrong before, or it is wrong now; document the intended contract and pick one.

issues.description: Inline `from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE` inside RPC function — module boundary leakage
issues.detail: get_default_base_image performs the import inside the function body. The top of nb.py is the natural place to declare what this module depends on; an inline import hides the dependency from anyone reading the module's interface. Move the import to the top of the file unless there is a documented circular-import reason. The RPC module's boundary should declare its dependencies plainly.

issues.description: Button width style 'width: 5%' is suspect on a contained Button with text 'IMAGE'
issues.detail: The new IMAGE button has `style={{ width: '5%' }}`. 5% of the parent will not accommodate the word 'IMAGE' in most layouts; this is likely either a leftover or a styling bug. The wrapping div uses 'padding: 0, marginRight: 4px' which also suggests the styling intent was not fully worked out. Audit the rendered result and replace with a documented width or remove the inline style.

issues.description: No test coverage added for the new RPC endpoint, the resolution chain, or the LSP-affected pipeline change
issues.detail: A new RPC (get_default_base_image), a changed Pipeline postcondition, and a four-level frontend resolution chain (step.baseImage -> pipelineBaseImage -> defaultBaseImage -> hardcoded literal) ship without tests. The contract is exactly the kind of thing tests pin down: 'when no image is set anywhere, the rendered DSL component receives python:3.12'; 'when pipeline metadata has base_image X, step cells without their own image inherit X'. Without these, the resolution order is folklore.

review.summary: The PR's core abstraction — 'the system's default base image' — is the right thing to name, but the implementation fails the single-source-of-truth contract: the literal 'python:3.12' is declared in three places (Python constant, TS frontend constant, TS Commands fallback) and will drift. More serious is a quiet postcondition change in Pipeline._set_base_image: '' (sentinel for 'unset, let downstream decide') has been replaced with the concrete default, collapsing the distinction between 'no image determined' and 'default image chosen' for every consumer of Pipeline.base_image. The frontend resolution chain (step -> pipeline -> default -> hardcoded) now has overlapping defaulting layers with the template, creating ambiguity about where the contract lives. Smaller issues: the edit-base-image precondition was tightened (requires stepName) without justification; createBaseImageText's visual contract widened to always render; an inline import hides a module dependency; no tests pin down the new resolution order. Recommend: centralize DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE in one place (backend, fetched via RPC), revert the pipeline.py sentinel change OR document and enforce the new invariant, and remove redundant defaulting rungs in the template.
